reference.title: Barbell Glute Bridge (hands on bar)
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in on the floor, breathe out as the hips rise, hold briefly at the top, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.8 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen; use a bar pad and plates big enough to roll the bar over the hips. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Heavier bar, then the barbell hip thrust from a bench.

cues.text: Lie on the floor, bar (with a pad) rolled over the hip crease, hands holding the bar just outside the hips. Feet flat about hip width, heels about a foot from the buttocks.
Brace, press through the heels and lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, ribs down, no arch in the lower back.
Lower the hips slowly back to the floor; the plates take the bar.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop when the hips line up with the shoulders and knees; ribs down.
Press through the heels; move the feet closer if the hamstrings cramp.
Push the knees out over the feet.
Hold it on the hip crease with both hands.

kinematics.norm: From about 40-50 degrees on the floor to neutral at the top (Boren 2011)
About 90 degrees at the top (common coaching)
Shoulders, hips and knees in line at the top (common coaching)
Bar across the hip crease, padded; large plates leave room to roll under (common coaching)
Pause at the top, slow lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Glute Bridge (hands on bar), video (movement reference only)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Use a thick bar pad over the hips and large-diameter plates so the bar rolls over the hips.
Keep the head and shoulders relaxed on the mat.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hip-bone discomfort: thicker pad, lighter bar.
Hamstring cramps: feet closer to the buttocks.
progressions: Barbell hip thrust from a bench.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor; the bridge works the glutes through the top of the hip-extension range (Contreras 2015; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor; the bridge works the glutes through the top of the hip-extension range (Contreras 2015; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; less active with the knees bent about 90 degrees at the top.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; less active with the knees bent about 90 degrees at the top.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knee angle so the hips, not the knees, do the work.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the knee angle so the hips, not the knees, do the work.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips and keep the knees from flaring.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips and keep the knees from flaring.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the knees over the feet.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the knees over the feet.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the ribs down so the lower back does not arch at the top.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine neutral; the movement should come from the hips, not the lower back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine neutral; the movement should come from the hips, not the lower back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the bar in place on the hips.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the bar in place on the hips.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Help pin the bar to the hips with straight arms.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Help pin the bar to the hips with straight arms.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Press down on the bar to steady it.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Press down on the bar to steady it.

phases.label: Hips on the floor, bar on the hips

guides.label: Hips rise to line up with knees and shoulders
